claims.claim: The king proposed launching two convicted criminals as the first passengers
claims.quote: The king proposed to launch two convicted criminals, but it is most likely that the inventors decided to send a sheep, a duck, and a rooster aloft first.

claims.claim: The king in question was Louis XVI
claims.quote: The demonstration was performed at the royal palace in Versailles, before King Louis XVI and Queen Marie Antoinette and a crowd.

claims.claim: The inventors most likely overruled the king's proposal
claims.quote: but it is most likely that the inventors decided to send a sheep, a duck, and a rooster aloft first

claims.claim: The tethered-flight image is by Claude Louis Desrais, 1783
claims.quote:
Date: 1783-10-19
Author: Claude Louis Desrais

claims.claim: Joseph thought smoke held a gas he called "levity"
claims.quote: contained within it a special gas, which he called "Montgolfier Gas", with a special property he called levity

claims.claim: Joseph got the idea from laundry billowing over a fire
claims.quote: He first contemplated building machines when he observed laundry drying over a fire incidentally form pockets that billowed upwards.

claims.claim: He burned wool and hay as fuel
claims.quote: On 14 December 1782 they conducted their first test flight, using ignited wool and hay as fuel.

claims.claim: He named the buoyant substance "Montgolfier Gas"
claims.quote: he believed that the smoke itself was the buoyant part and contained within it a special gas, which he called "Montgolfier Gas"

claims.claim: The plate showing inflation over a fire comes from the Venice 1784 edition of Faujas de Saint-Fond
claims.quote: Illustration from: B. Faujas de Saint-Fond:  Descrizione delle esperienze della macchina aerostatica dei Signori di Montgolfier. Traduzione dal Francese , Venice, Graziosi, 1784

claims.claim: The December 1782 device flew (nearly) three kilometres and was then destroyed by a bystander
claims.quote: The device floated nearly three kilometers (1.9 mi) but was destroyed after landing by the "indiscretion" of a bypasser.

claims.claim: In December 1782 the lift was so strong the brothers lost control
claims.quote: The lifting force was so great that they lost control of their craft.

claims.claim: The record blames the "indiscretion" of a passerby
claims.quote: destroyed after landing by the "indiscretion" of a bypasser

claims.claim: The Champ de Mars image is a vue d'optique of 1783
claims.quote: Vue d'optique shows the Montgolfier brothers' balloon, "The Globe," ascending from Champ de Mars, Paris, France, August 27, 1783.

claims.claim: Pilâtre took off his coat to stop the fire mid-flight
claims.quote: As it appeared it could destroy the balloon, Pilâtre took off his coat to stop the fire.

claims.claim: The first free flight by humans was on 21 November 1783, covering nine kilometres over Paris
claims.quote: On 21 November 1783, the first free flight by humans was made by Pilâtre de Rozier, together with an army officer, the marquis d'Arlandes... They flew about 900 metres (3,000 ft) above Paris for a distance of nine kilometers.

claims.claim: Burning embers scorched the fabric and were daubed out with sponges
claims.quote: However, burning embers from the fire were scorching the balloon fabric and had to be daubed out with sponges.

claims.claim: The hand-coloured aerostatic globe plate dates from 1786
claims.quote: Description: 1786 description of the historic Montgolfier Brothers' 1783 balloon flight.  Illustration with engineering proportions and description.

claims.claim: The flights were paid for by public subscription
claims.quote: establishing public subscriptions to fundraise for their experiments in hydrogen and hot air balloon technologies

claims.claim: Faujas de Saint-Fond gathered first-hand accounts, letters, tables and diagrams into one book
claims.quote: Barthélemy Faujas de Saint-Fond’s Description des expériences assembles first-hand observations, research, technical descriptions, letters, tables, diagrams, and illustrations related to the groundbreaking experiments in balloon flight in the 1780's.

claims.claim: Faujas de Saint-Fond's book was published in Paris in 1783
claims.quote: A PARIS, Chez CUCHET, rue & hôtel Serpente. M. DCC. LXXXIII.

claims.claim: No criminals flew; a sheep, a duck and a rooster did
claims.quote: On 19 September 1783, the Aérostat Réveillon was flown with the first living beings in a basket attached to the balloon: a sheep called Montauciel ("Climb-to-the-sky"), a duck and a rooster.

claims.claim: The animal flight lasted about eight minutes and covered three kilometres, landing safely
claims.quote: The flight lasted approximately eight minutes, covered three kilometres (1.9 mi), and obtained an altitude of about 500 metres (1,600 ft). The craft landed safely after flying.

claims.claim: All three animals were unharmed
claims.quote: le Mouton le Coq et le Canard n'éprouverent pas la plus légère incommodité

claims.claim: The Versailles engraving was published by Le Noir in Paris, 1783
claims.quote: Éditeur : A Paris chez Le Noir Md. Fournisseur du Cabinet des Estampes du Roi demeurant au Louvre

claims.claim: The first hot air balloon flight carried animals rather than a person
claims.where: caption opening ("Who was on the first hot air balloon flight? Not a person.")
claims.quote: On 4 June 1783, they flew the balloon at Annonay in front of a group of dignitaries from the états particuliers. The flight covered 2 km (1.2 mi), lasted 10 minutes

claims.claim: The criminals were proposed in order to test whether the upper air was survivable
claims.quote: There was some concern about the effects of flight into the upper atmosphere on living creatures. The king proposed to launch two convicted criminals

claims.claim: The sheep was called Montauciel, "Climb-to-the-sky"
claims.quote: a sheep called Montauciel ("Climb-to-the-sky")

claims.claim: The Versailles demonstration on 19 September 1783 took place before the king and Marie Antoinette
claims.quote: The demonstration was performed at the royal palace in Versailles, before King Louis XVI and Queen Marie Antoinette and a crowd.

claims.claim: Joseph Montgolfier was a paper manufacturer from Annonay
claims.quote: were aviation pioneers, balloonists and paper manufacturers from the commune Annonay in Ardèche, France

claims.claim: After the animals survived, the king allowed flights with humans
claims.quote: Since the animals survived, the king allowed flights with humans.

claims.claim: It remains only "most likely" that the inventors, not the king, chose the animals
claims.quote: but it is most likely that the inventors decided to send a sheep, a duck, and a rooster aloft first

claims.claim: Some credit the priest Bartolomeu de Gusmão with inventing the hot air balloon 74 years earlier
claims.quote: Some claim that the hot air balloon was invented about 74 years earlier by the Brazilian/Portuguese priest Bartolomeu de Gusmão.

claims.claim: The Fédération Aéronautique Internationale does not recognise the Gusmão claim
claims.quote: However, this claim is not generally recognized by aviation historians outside the Portuguese-speaking community, in particular the Fédération Aéronautique Internationale.

claims.claim: The Le Noir engraving's caption claims more than 130,000 spectators
claims.quote: EXPÉRIENCE AÉROSTATIQUE Faite à Versailles le 19. Septembre 1783. en présence de leurs Majestés, de la Famille Royale et de plus de 130. milles Spectateurs
